sections.markdown:
## C2 — Headlight, power steering and accelerator failures, fuel saving, and confusables: phone rules by age, presumed impairment versus arrest, test fail levels by age, and failure responses
Continuation facts for the remaining equipment failures and fuel saving followed by confusable pairs, each tied to one manual page; knowledge-graph hints (group, difficulty, confusable pair) sit only in the trailing Why it matters line of each block.

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A06
If your headlights go out, flip the headlight switch off and on, then try your high beams, driving lights or hazard lights, which may give enough light to steer off the road. [A06]
Why it matters: group equipment failures; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A06
After a headlight failure, slow down and ease onto the shoulder. [A06]
Why it matters: group equipment failures; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A06
If power steering fails, grip the wheel firmly because steering will be hard, then slow down and ease onto the shoulder. [A06]
Why it matters: group equipment failures; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A06
If the accelerator sticks, look for an escape path and shift into neutral, using an open palm on the shifter so you do not push it into another gear. [A06]
Why it matters: group equipment failures; continuation; difficulty hard.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A06
With a stuck accelerator, steer smoothly while braking and leave the road once it is safe. [A06]
Why it matters: group equipment failures; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A07
To save fuel, drive at a steady pace without going over posted limits, and avoid jackrabbit starts and sudden stops. [A07]
Why it matters: group fuel saving; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A07
Other fuel savers are cutting unneeded idling, combining errands into one trip and keeping the vehicle properly maintained. [A07]
Why it matters: group fuel saving; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A01
A driver under 18 may not use a phone at all while driving, while a driver 18 or older may use one only through a hands-free accessory. [A01]
Why it matters: group distraction; confusable under-age rule versus adult rule; difficulty hard.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A03
At a BAC of 0.08% or more the law presumes impairment, yet a driver below 0.08% can still be arrested for DUII if alcohol or drugs are affecting their driving. [A03]
Why it matters: group impairment; confusable presumed impairment versus arrest threshold; difficulty hard.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A04
The implied consent fail level is any amount of alcohol for a driver under 21 but 0.08 percent or more for a driver 21 or older. [A04]
Why it matters: group impairment; confusable under twenty-one versus twenty-one and over; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A04
Refusing the implied consent test is not a way out, since refusal itself can bring a fine and a suspension of driving privileges. [A04]
Why it matters: group impairment; confusable taking the test versus refusing it; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A04
Open alcohol containers should ride in the trunk, and a bottle whose seal has been broken counts as open even after it is recapped. [A04]
Why it matters: group open container; confusable sealed versus resealed; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A05
Riding outside the cab is discouraged for everyone but outlawed for anyone under 18, while a dog may ride outside only when a carrier or framework keeps it from falling. [A05]
Why it matters: group external passengers; confusable adults versus minors versus dogs; difficulty hard.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A05
A front blowout shows up as hard steering and a pull to one side, while a rear blowout shows up as weaving or swaying of the back end; the response is the same: grip, slow gradually, pull off. [A05]
Why it matters: group blowouts; confusable front versus rear blowout; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A06
Failed brakes call for pumping the pedal and downshifting, whereas a stuck accelerator calls for shifting to neutral and braking while steering smoothly. [A06]
Why it matters: group equipment failures; confusable brake failure versus stuck accelerator; difficulty hard.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0093]
